Flower 48

Japanese flower cards: 12 monthly suits, 48 cards. The Hanafuda deck (48 cards, 12 monthly suits) supports 4 games: Koi-Koi, Hana-Awase, Go-Stop, and Oicho-Kabu. All involve matching and collecting cards by suit or type.

4 Variants
flower-48 Plugin
✓ Frontmatter-only

Declared, Not Coded

Every rule of Flower 48 below is frontmatter in the rules corpus. The board beside each is the game itself, live.

Go-Stop Rules

Korean hanafuda variant played with the Hwatu deck. The most popular card game in South Korea. Match cards from hand to field by month; collect scoring combinations. Core mechanic: after reaching the threshold, declare 'Stop' to collect winnings or 'Go' to press on for bigger rewards at the risk of penalty if another player stops first.

engine:
  topology:
    type: tableau
    layout: radial
  players: [player1, player2]
  plugins:
    flower-48:
      game: fishing
      scoring: go-stop
      cardsEach:
        2: 10
        3: 7
      field:
        2: 8
        3: 6
      goThreshold:
        2: 7
        3: 3
      chips:
        start: 100
      rounds: 6
      options:
        rounds:
          label: Hands
          values: [3, 6, 12]

Go-Stop

Hana-Awase Rules

The base Hanafuda matching game. No yaku — card values only. Simplest entry point to the deck.

engine:
  topology:
    type: tableau
    layout: radial
  players: [player1, player2, player3]
  plugins:
    flower-48:
      game: fishing
      scoring: points
      cardsEach:
        2: 8
        3: 7
        4: 5
      field:
        2: 8
        3: 6
        4: 8
      cardValues:
        hikari: 20
        tane: 10
        tanzaku: 5
        kasu: 1
      partnerships:
        - [player1, player3]
        - [player2, player4]
      rounds: 1
